- **The check binds both dispositions symmetrically**, which newly binds the pre-existing waive heading. The waive prose therefore moves to state the wrapped `<!-- gaia-debt-key: … -->` grammar its entries are now judged by, rather than only "its dedup key". Narrowing the check to the new heading instead would have restored the exact asymmetry this change exists to remove.
- **Two Suggestions.** The key extraction now anchors on the full `<!-- gaia-debt-key:` opener rather than the bare literal, with a new test pinning that body prose merely mentioning the key injects no path; and a guard that validated one `jq` read while assigning a second now reads once.
- `.claude/skills/gaia/references/residue.md:42` — "the emit does not say which" is stated absolutely, while `total_keyed_count` is a one-way discriminator: an emit carrying `gh_ok: false` with `total_keyed_count` above zero can only be the issue-read arm. The guidance the sentence supports is correct, and the field never reaches the operator on that arm, but a maintainer who later greps the emit finds the discriminator and reads the prose as false. Tightening the absolute to a reliability claim settles it. <!-- gaia-debt-key: v1 class=holistic/overclaimed-guarantee path=.claude/skills/gaia/references/residue.md line=42 -->
- `.gaia/cli/src/residue/tally.ts:51` — the `--count-only` flag description says "No head fetch, no git call", but `resolveRoot` reaches `resolveRepoRoot`, which always executes one `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`. The claim is true of the per-candidate resolution step it has in mind and false as written, so a reader sizing the statusline refresher's per-tick subprocess cost undercounts it. <!-- gaia-debt-key: v1 class=holistic/overclaimed-guarantee path=.gaia/cli/src/residue/tally.ts line=51 -->
- `.gaia/cli/src/residue/tally.ts:60` (and the same claim at `:12`) — `HELP_TEXT` and the module docblock name the merged-PR window as the only read that sets `gh_ok: false`, but the tech-debt issue read sets it too. An operator running `--help` to interpret `gh_ok: false` during a partial outage is pointed at a call that may have succeeded. The remedial action is the same either way (re-run `residue-tally`), and the file's own comment at `:280` already carries the correct two-arm wording to borrow. This is the sibling of the skill-copy defect repaired in this branch's round-5 commit, which landed on the prose and left the CLI copy behind. <!-- gaia-debt-key: v1 class=holistic/partial-cause-reporting path=.gaia/cli/src/residue/tally.ts line=60 -->
- `.gaia/cli/src/wiki/diff-size.ts:142` — `sumWikiLinesAtRef` spawns one `git cat-file -p` per blob, 188 of them at HEAD, so each `computeDiffSize` call on the CI merge gate spawns 188 git processes. No live failure; cost is linear in vault size and a single `git cat-file --batch` would do it in one. Pre-existing, latent at the fork point, and untouched by this change. `<!-- gaia-debt-key: v1 class=holistic/repeated-round-trip path=.gaia/cli/src/wiki/diff-size.ts line=142 -->`
- `.gaia/hook-capabilities.json:36` — the `why` field attributes `network` to this hook's own `gh pr view` alone, while the foreign-repo permit arm reaches the repo-scope helper's `gh repo view` before any body read happens. A maintainer sizing the hook's network surface concludes that arm is offline, and one who narrowed away the body read would conclude `network` can be dropped. Latent at the fork point: this pull request edits a later clause of the same sentence and leaves this one as it stands. <!-- gaia-debt-key: v1 class=holistic/partial-cause-reporting path=.gaia/hook-capabilities.json line=36 -->
